proof.text: Put $F_q=\{q\}\times_QE$. A horn in $F_q$ is a horn in $E$ over the constant simplex at $q$; a lift for $p$ therefore lies in $F_q$. Thus $F_q$ is Kan. By [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre], $P=|p|:|E|\to|Q|$ is a Serre fibration. By [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], its k-space fiber at the realized vertex $q$ is canonically $|F_q|$. These theorems use exactly the all-horn lifting condition in the statement and the realization of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. If $Q$ has no vertices, it has no simplices, since every simplex has a vertex; the map $p$ then forces $E$ empty as well. In this case $p$ is the identity of the empty simplicial set, and both assertions hold. Below allow disconnected spaces but assume $Q$ nonempty.

proof.text: We record explicitly why checking homotopy groups at vertices suffices. Every point of a realization is represented in a simplex and is joined to any vertex of that simplex by its straight-line barycentric path. For a path $\gamma$ from $x$ to $y$ and a based cube map $h:([-1,1]^r,\partial[-1,1]^r)\to(T,x)$, write $\rho=\max_j|t_j|$ and replace $h$ by $h(2t)$ for $\rho\leq\tfrac12$ and by $\gamma(2\rho-1)$ for $\rho\geq\tfrac12$. The formulas agree on the common boundary and give a cube based at $y$. Applying the same formula to homotopies makes this a map on based homotopy classes. Reversing $\gamma$ gives its inverse: the two collars trace $\gamma$ followed by its reverse, which contracts by shortening the distance traveled along $\gamma$, and rescaling the inner cube removes the remaining constant collar. This construction commutes with postcomposition. Thus the maps on based homotopy groups at two endpoints of a path are related by bijections commuting with every continuous map. In particular bijectivity of the homomorphisms induced by $P$ at vertex basepoints gives isomorphisms at all basepoints; the same observation applies to each $|F_q|$. All these constructions use the cubical homotopy and realization definitions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

proof.text: Suppose $p$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Fix a vertex $q$ of $Q$. Surjectivity on components gives a point $e_0\in|E|$ and a path from $P(e_0)$ to $q$. Path lifting in [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence] supplies an endpoint in $|F_q|$, so the fiber is nonempty and hence has a vertex $e$ (a representative of any realization point has simplex vertices). The orbit set of the $\pi_1(|Q|,q)$-action on $\pi_0(|F_q|)$ is the set of total-space components over the component of $q$, by that same cited statement. It is a singleton since $\pi_0(P)$ is bijective. The stabilizer of the component of $e$ is the image of $\pi_1(|E|,e)\to\pi_1(|Q|,q)$, which is the whole group since $p$ is a weak equivalence. The orbit of this component is therefore a singleton; since it is the only orbit, $\pi_0(|F_q|)$ itself is a singleton. This checks connectedness of the entire fiber, not just the distinguished component.

proof.text: Still assuming $p$ a weak equivalence, choose any vertex $e$ of $F_q$ and any $r\geq1$. The sequence of [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence] contains $\pi_{r+1}(|E|,e)\to\pi_{r+1}(|Q|,q)\xrightarrow{\delta}\pi_r(|F_q|,e)\xrightarrow{i_*}\pi_r(|E|,e)\xrightarrow{P_*}\pi_r(|Q|,q)$. Surjectivity of the first map forces $\delta=0$, so exactness makes $i_*$ injective. Injectivity of the last map gives $\operatorname{im}i_*=\ker P_*=0$, hence $\pi_r(|F_q|,e)=0$. This argument also works for the possibly nonabelian group in degree one. Step 2 extends the vanishing to every basepoint. Together with step 3, the definition of weak contractibility in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] says that $F_q$ is weakly contractible.

proof.text: Conversely assume every $F_q$ is weakly contractible. Then each $|F_q|$ is nonempty and has exactly one path component. Every component of $|Q|$ contains a vertex by step 2, so choosing a point of $|F_q|$ proves surjectivity of $\pi_0(P)$. For injectivity, fix a vertex $q$ in a base component. The orbit formula of [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence] identifies the set of all total-space components over that base component with the orbit set of $\pi_1(|Q|,q)$ on the singleton $\pi_0(|F_q|)$. That orbit set is a singleton. There is consequently exactly one total-space component over each base component, proving bijectivity of $\pi_0(P)$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.16, with the path-lifting component argument of Proposition 2.4.18 and its orbit formulation in the cited node. Online source read; archival copy WANTED. The displayed details are agent-written.

proof.text: Let $e$ be any vertex of $E$ and $q=p(e)$. Since $F_q$ is weakly contractible, $\pi_r(|F_q|,e)=0$ for every $r\geq1$, and $\pi_0(|F_q|)$ is a singleton. Exactness in [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence] at $\pi_r(|E|,e)$ makes $P_*$ injective for every $r\geq1$, since its kernel is the image of the zero group $\pi_r(|F_q|,e)$. For $r\geq2$, exactness at $\pi_r(|Q|,q)$ makes $P_*$ surjective since the next group $\pi_{r-1}(|F_q|,e)$ is zero. For $r=1$ the connecting map lands in the singleton $\pi_0(|F_q|)$, so pointed-set exactness gives the same surjectivity. Thus $P_*$ is an isomorphism at every vertex basepoint. Step 2 transfers this to every basepoint of $|E|$; step 5 supplies the component bijection. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $p$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This proves the reverse implication and the claimed equivalence.

title: Kan fibrations are equivalences exactly when their fibers are contractible
statement: Use spaces, horns, weak homotopy equivalences and weak contractibility as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A Kan fibration is a simplicial map with the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ with $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$ (outer horns included). Let $p:E\to Q$ be a Kan fibration between small Kan complexes. Then $p$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if every strict fiber $\{q\}\times_Q E$ over a vertex $q\in Q$ is weakly contractible.

The statement is Kerodon Proposition 3.3.7.6, conditions (3) iff (4), restricted to Kan fibrations between Kan complexes. The horn convention and weak contractibility (which includes a nonempty fiber) match def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones. No target or coefficient category is involved. Step 1: the fiber is Kan by lifting over the constant simplex; the realized map is a Serre fibration by lem-coef-kan-realization-serre; its fiber is |F_q| as a k-space by lem-coef-realization-finite-limits; an empty base forces an empty total space. Step 2 is an elementary change of basepoint along a path in a collar; I checked the formulas where the pieces meet, and they commute with postcomposition. Step 3 uses path lifting plus the orbit and stabilizer clauses of lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence to show the whole fiber is connected. Step 4 shows every positive homotopy group of the fiber vanishes, including degree 1. Step 5 gives the bijection on components with no connectedness assumption on the base. Step 6 gives injectivity and surjectivity in every positive degree, using pointed-set exactness in degree 1. Every step uses only what the cited statements say. The dependency closure is acyclic, the three cited lemmas are in the item's own unit, and no tool uses are needed. Small cases (empty spaces, an empty fiber, a two-point fiber, a fiber with nonzero pi_2, a discrete base) all behave correctly. There are no new nodes and no fixes were needed.
